title: The Arcadia Ballroom and meeting Toots Mondello
summary: At the Arcadia in 1929 he heard Mal Hallett's band and first met saxophonist Toots Mondello.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: That was another name that Mills used. You know. All right. So you are now in the early thirties, a published composer, alto instrumentalist, trumpet instrumentalist, arranger -- and you had even had a band of your own for a short period, I think in 1929, as you mentioned, at the Arcadia Ballroom on 53rd Street and Broadway.
Who were some of the bands that played at the Arcadia? I guess there were mor than one -- at the time you were there.
I remember one, and there were certainly more -- but I do remember that there was Mal Hallett, and there was a saxophone player with him that I liked particularly -- and that was 'Toots' Mondello.

That's when I first met Toots. And we struck up and maintained a very nice association through the years. I don't see much of him these days; he's on the West Coast and I'm on the East Coast, or rather, vise versa.
Well, you're on the East Coast now.
I'm on the East Coast now, but so is he.
There were certainly other orchestras, but I don't remember who they were.
